What a /18 means

A /18 holds 16,384 addresses. Blocks this size are usually site or data-centre allocations that get divided into smaller subnets.

The prefix length is the number of leading bits that identify the network. A /18 uses 18 network bits and leaves 14 host bits, so the block contains 16,384 addresses. Usable hosts: 2(32−18) − 2 = 16,384 − 2 = 16,382.

Configuration examples

Cisco IOS

interface Vlan10
 ip address 172.16.0.1 255.255.192.0
!
access-list 10 permit 172.16.0.0 0.0.63.255

Juniper Junos

set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 172.16.0.1/18

Linux

ip addr add 172.16.0.1/18 dev eth0

Addresses shown are examples from private or documentation space. Replace them with your own plan.

FAQ

How many usable hosts are in a /18?

16,382. A /18 has 16,384 addresses; the first is the network address and the last is the broadcast address, so 16,382 are usable.

What is the subnet mask for /18?

255.255.192.0. The wildcard mask, used in ACLs and OSPF network statements, is 0.0.63.255.
